question: A mine winder operator needs the total figure, in kilonewtons, for the winder house. Each skip's rate of change of speed a, in m/s^2, is the larger value satisfying a^2 - 9a + 20 = 0. A skip has a mass of 68000 g, and the winder supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion. The house sheet expresses that force in kilonewtons and adds a standing rope tension of 7 kN. Each drum carries 2 skips, and the house has 9 identical drums. What total figure, in kN, does the house sheet show?

A test-house engineer needs the final entry, in kilonewtons, for a shaker rig. The rig's base rate r, in m/s^2, is the smaller value satisfying r^2 - 13r + 40 = 0, and the amplifier drives the table at 7 times that base rate. The table has a mass of 119 kg, and the shaker supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion. The entry expresses that force in kilonewtons and then adds a fixed frame pre-load of 30 kN. A guide bearing finally relieves 14 kN of the entry. What is the final entry, in kN?

A cable-machine shop is setting up a matched pair of pulleys. One pulley has 319 grooves and the other has 128 grooves, and the setter needs the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly, since that fixes the indexing step. The test carriage's rate of change of speed, in m/s^2, is then set numerically equal to that number. The carriage has a mass of 124 kg, the shop floor sits at 20 degrees C, and the drive supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion. The rating sheet expresses that force in kilonewtons, then adds 4 kN for the frame pre-load, 23 kN for the hydraulic clamp and a further 15 kN for the counterweight. What figure, in kN, does the rating sheet show?

A bearing works needs the total energy, in joules, held by all its test spindles at one instant. Two index rings on the rig carry 348 teeth and 271 teeth, and the setter needs the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly. Each test slider is run at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to that number, and a slider has a mass of 15000 g. The energy one slider carries by virtue of its motion is multiplied by the 5 sliders on a spindle. A rig holds 3 spindles, a bay holds 12 rigs, and the works has 8 identical bays. What total energy, in J, do the spindles hold?

A test range measures a small sabot launched along a rail. The launcher drives the sabot with 2 identical coils, and each coil contributes 8 m/s while it charges and a further 2 m/s while it discharges. A trailing spring then adds another 25 m/s, and the sabot leaves the rail at the accumulated speed. The sabot has a mass of 4000 g. The bench measures the energy it carries by virtue of that motion, subtracts 27 J for the rail friction and a further 26 J for the muzzle seal. What is the bench's corrected reading, in kJ?

A pneumatics laboratory releases a piston along a short bore. The piston's release speed, in metres per second, is the area under the curve 5*x^2 + 3*x between x = 0 and x = 1, where x is the valve-opening fraction. The piston has a mass of 10000 g, and the laboratory air is held at 23 degrees C. The energy the piston carries by virtue of that motion is expressed in kilojoules, and a standing rig overhead of 6 kJ is subtracted from it. The laboratory fires 11 pistons in a rack and runs 6 identical racks. What is the laboratory's net total, in kJ?

A paper mill needs the figure, in kilonewtons, that goes on its reel-drive sheet. Two change gears on the drive carry 192 teeth and 200 teeth, and the setter needs the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly. The reel carriage's rate of change of speed, in m/s^2, is set numerically equal to that number, and the carriage has a mass of 107 kg. Each drive supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion, and the mill runs 5 identical drives. The sheet expresses their combined force in kilonewtons and then adds a standing web tension of 23 kN. What figure, in kN, goes on the sheet?

A textile mill is rating a new beam drive. Two change wheels carry 286 teeth and 172 teeth, and the setter needs the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly. The beam carriage's rate of change of speed, in m/s^2, is set numerically equal to that number, and the carriage has a mass of 10 kg. Each drive supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion. A frame holds 4 identical drives, a loom holds 3 frames, a hall holds 12 looms, and the mill has 8 identical halls. What total force, in N, do the mill's beam drives supply?

A rolling-stock depot needs the net figure, in kilojoules, for a shunting trial. Two index wheels on the test rig carry 330 teeth and 284 teeth, and the setter needs the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly. Each test wagon is then run at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to that number, and a wagon has a mass of 57000 g. The energy one wagon carries by virtue of that motion is expressed in kilojoules, and a rake holds 11 identical wagons. The trial covers 8 identical rakes, and a standing depot overhead of 18 kJ is subtracted from the total. What is the net figure, in kJ?

A hydraulic press is being rated on the shop floor. The ram's rate of change of speed, in m/s^2, is the area under the curve 5*x^2 + 7*x between x = 0 and x = 2, where x is the valve-lift index, and the shop is held at 27 degrees C. The ram has a mass of 9 kg, and the press supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion. A guide gland absorbs 15 N of that force, and the remainder is expressed in kilonewtons. A standing frame relief of 9 kN is then subtracted from that figure. What is the press's net rating, in kN?

A gear-cutting shop needs the net figure, in kilojoules, at the foot of its test sheet. Two index plates carry 154 holes and 380 holes, and the setter needs the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly. The test slider is then run at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to that number, and the slider has a mass of 35 kg. To the energy the slider carries by virtue of that motion the sheet adds 29 J for the latch, then subtracts 29 J for the release, and expresses the result in kilojoules. A standing instrument allowance of 30 kJ is finally subtracted. What is the net figure, in kJ?

A cable-car maker needs the total pull, in kilonewtons, on a haul frame. Two index wheels carry 271 teeth and 367 teeth, and the setter needs the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly. The gearbox then drives the carriage at 5 times that number, in m/s^2, and the carriage has a mass of 14000 g. Each drive supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion, and a frame holds 6 identical drives. The frame's combined force is expressed in kilonewtons, and the installation has 5 identical frames. What total pull, in kN, does the installation carry?

A container terminal needs the net figure, in kilonewtons, for a spreader trial. The spreader's rate of change of speed a, in m/s^2, is the smaller value satisfying a^2 - 12a + 35 = 0. The spreader has a mass of 174000 g, and the hoist supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion. That force is expressed in kilonewtons, and the terminal runs 10 identical spreaders. A standing gantry relief of 20 kN is subtracted from their combined figure, and a lashing pre-load of 2 kN is then added. What is the net figure, in kN?

A shipyard needs the net figure, in joules, for a launch-ways trial. The cradle's release speed, in metres per second, is the area under the curve 2*x^2 + 0*x between x = 0 and x = 4, where x is the slipway station index. The cradle has a mass of 36 kg, and the energy it carries by virtue of that motion is the base figure for one release. The trial covers 6 releases on each of 2 identical ways. A standing instrument allowance of 27 J is then subtracted from the total. What is the net figure, in J?

A saw mill needs the total thrust, in newtons, from its feed system. The base rate b, in m/s^2, is the smaller value satisfying b^2 - 8*b + 12 = 0, and a control offset then adds a further 21, giving the feed carriage's actual rate of change of speed in m/s^2. The carriage has a mass of 41 kg, and the mill floor is at 17 degrees C. Each feed unit supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion. A saw line carries 6 identical feed units, and the mill runs 10 identical lines. What total thrust, in N, does the mill's feed system deliver?

A rescue-equipment laboratory drops a weight down a guided shaft. The weight's nominal release speed, in metres per second, is the area under the curve 2*x^2 + 6*x between x = 1 and x = 4, where x is the release-cam index. A catch mechanism then removes 7 m/s from that nominal figure, so the weight falls at what remains. The weight has a mass of 4 kg. The laboratory measures the energy the weight carries by virtue of that motion and deducts 8 J for the guide friction. What is the corrected figure, in kJ?

A pump works is setting up an index drive on the bench. Two timing wheels carry 142 teeth and 256 teeth, and the fitter needs the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly. The test slider is then run at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to that number, and the slider has a mass of 16000 g. The energy the slider carries by virtue of its motion is multiplied by the 8 sliders on the bench, and the bench total is expressed in kilojoules. A charged capacitor bank contributes a further 5 kJ to that bench total. The works operates 5 identical benches. What total figure, in kJ, does the works hold?

A packaging machine's pusher travels along a guide, and its distance travelled is, in metres, 4*t^3 + 0*t^2 with t in seconds. The engineers read the pusher's speed at the instant t = 1 s, and the gearing means the carriage itself moves at 6 times that speed. The carriage has a mass of 14000 g. From the energy the carriage carries by virtue of its motion, 21 J is deducted for the guide friction. Each machine has 7 identical carriages, and the plant runs 12 identical machines. What total energy, in J, does the plant hold at that instant?

A vehicle proving ground is commissioning a sled drive. The sled's rate of change of speed a, in m/s^2, is the smaller value satisfying a^2 - 5a + 6 = 0. The sled has a mass of 43 kg, and the control room is at 18 degrees C. The drive supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion, and the commissioning sheet expresses that force in kilonewtons. Each track runs 2 identical sleds, and the ground has 10 identical tracks. What total force, in kN, do the ground's sled drives supply?

A laboratory needs the final entry, in kilojoules, for a spring-launcher trial. The launcher's raw index is the area under the curve 2*x^2 + 7*x between x = 1 and x = 2, where x is the cam setting. The calibration then subtracts 20 from that raw index and adds a further 13 to what remains, and the result is the projectile's launch speed in metres per second. The projectile has a mass of 4 kg, and the bench sits at 21 degrees C. The entry records the energy the projectile carries by virtue of that motion. What is the final entry, in kJ?

A propulsion laboratory needs the final entry, in kilojoules, for one test firing. The trolley's release speed, in metres per second, is the area under the curve 4*x^2 + 8*x between x = 0 and x = 1, where x is the throttle fraction. The trolley has a mass of 41 kg, and the test cell sits at 27 degrees C. The energy the trolley carries by virtue of that motion is expressed in kilojoules. A standing rig overhead of 28 kJ is subtracted from it, and a charged accumulator then adds 11 kJ. What is the final entry, in kJ?

A mining contractor needs the total thrust, in kilonewtons, from a complete drill installation. The drill carriage's rate of change of speed, in m/s^2, is the area under the curve 5*x^2 + 2*x between x = 1 and x = 2, where x is the feed-lever index. The carriage has a mass of 85 kg, and each drill supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion, recorded in kilonewtons. A boom carries 5 identical drills, a rig carries 8 booms, and the installation has 3 identical rigs. What total thrust, in kN, does the installation deliver?

A machine shop needs the net figure, in kilojoules, at the foot of its index sheet. Two dividing plates carry 198 holes and 166 holes, and the setter needs the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly. The test slider is then run at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to that number, and the slider has a mass of 41000 g. The energy the slider carries by virtue of that motion is expressed in kilojoules. A bearing allowance of 2 kJ and a standing instrument allowance of 27 kJ are then subtracted from it in turn. What is the net figure, in kJ?

A cycle-track laboratory needs the net figure, in kilojoules, for a coasting trial. The trolley's coasting speed v, in m/s, is the smaller value that satisfies v^2 - 7v + 12 = 0. The trolley has a mass of 52000 g, and the energy it carries by virtue of that motion is expressed in kilojoules. A standing rig overhead of 27 kJ is subtracted from that figure. A further instrument allowance of 16 kJ is then subtracted as well. What is the net figure, in kJ?

A tool maker is trialling a spring-loaded ejector. The ejector head has 6 possible port positions, and the trial starts from the number of distinct sets of 4 ports that could be opened together. From that number 10 is subtracted for the blocked patterns, and the result is the pellet's launch speed in metres per second. The pellet has a mass of 33000 g, and the bench sits at 17 degrees C. To the energy the pellet carries by virtue of that motion, 21 J is added for the latch, and 10 J is then deducted for the guide. The maker fires 9 identical ejectors. What total energy, in J, do the ejectors deliver?
